evidence.quote: Non-Pretreatment Program POTWs The two permits for the non-pretreatment POTWs are not consistent with respect to pretreatment program requirements. evidence.quote: Neither permit contains requirements at 122.42(b)(3) to provide information on (i) the quality and quantity of effluent introduced into the POTW, and (ii) any anticipated impact of the change on the quantity or quality of effluent to be discharged from the POTW. The Milton permit does not discuss the establishment of a pretreatment program, when required, nor does it require that the program will meet all reporting requirements of the Clean Water Act and 40 CFR Part 403 (as does the Lewes permit). Both permits for POTWs without approved pretreatment programs have standard reopener clauses, but they do not specifically mention that they could be reopened, if deemed necessary, to require a pretreatment program or local limit development, based on results of an industrial waste survey, new categorical standards, or industry changes. Also, the standard reopener clause does not include requirements at 40 CFR Part 122.62(a)(2) and 403.5(c)(2). The fact sheets for these permits do not specifically state that a pretreatment program is not required at this time, or state the reason why. Because the Lewes fact sheet says the permit contains “Special Condition No. 2 outlines the pretreatment program requirements applicable to this facility” and the Milton permit and fact sheet are silent on this issue, it is somewhat confusing as to whether the Lewes POTW is required to have a pretreatment program. question: Compare Milton’s supplied 2012 assessment and October 2019 replacement notice. What changed in the documentary plan and what cannot be inferred about performance or current nutrient compliance?
answer: The assessment describes old Front Street operations, 0.35 MGD design flow and 0.16 MGD average flow, retains older permit expiry/no nutrient-limit assertions, yet survey narrative reports a new 2011 permit and 48 month TN upgrade need. The 2019 notice proposes a new Sam Lucas Road facility treating 350,000 gpd, with membrane zones and ultraviolet treatment, but using the existing Broadkill River discharge location and DE 0021491 conditions. The equal design magnitudes are source design/proposal figures, not an observed flow change or higher permitted capacity. Compare plan/site/treatment wording as proposed changes, not completed upgrades or concentration reductions. These passages do not prove the new plant was built, old site closed, nutrient limits met, chlorine incident resolved or ownership changed. Primary approval/current permit and commissioning/DMR data remain necessary.

evidence.quote: Tidewater – Milton Regional Tidewater’s Milton Regional facility has a service area of 1.65 square miles and consists of one sewer district with 11 pump stations serving 1,285 households. The facility provides primary, secondary, and tertiary treatment and some solids handling. It has a surface water discharge to the Broadkill River and then to Delaware Bay (Watershed #22). The NPDES permit for this discharge (DE0021491) expired on December 31, 2009. No TN or TP permitted limits are applicable. The plant reported having had an instantaneous chlorine non-compliance incident because of equipment failure. The plant’s current design flow is 0.35 MGD, and the average daily flow is 0.16 MGD, or about 46 percent of design flow. Peak flow at the plant is 0.301. Tidewater – Milton Regional facility has experienced I/I issues. Tidewater has conducted assessments of bowls in manholes and repaired cleanouts; however, during a heavy rain event, flows may still increase by 50 percent. Tidewater is investigating manhole repairs, as needed and portions of the system have been evaluated using a video camera. Financial Analysis

question: Compare the revised 2021 Cannery collection-system permit and March 2025 temporary-holding application letter. Did construction approval prove completion, and are 29,000 GPD and 2,100 gpd comparable plant discharge limits?
answer: The 2021 instrument authorizes construction, with 29,000 GPD an estimated pump-station design based on 116 housing units, not a Milton plant discharge limit. The March 20, 2025 DBF letter for Double H instead says the Cannery pump station and force main are not completed and proposes approximately 2,100 gpd temporary storage within private gravity collection, with contracted hauling. It encloses an August 30, 2021 construction permit, linking this connected-system scope to the reviewed earlier instrument. Preserve the later applicant-reported incomplete condition and proposal, without finding the whole Milton replacement plant incomplete, granting a holding permit, or concluding unauthorized disposal/current violation from a nominal 2024 expiry. Expected design flow and interim proposed storage are different scopes, not observed discharge reductions or changed plant limits. Obtain extension/amendment, actual construction/as-built/acceptance and holding authorization/hauling records.
